mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep edging up from their current depressed levels, routine commuting and downtown errands will expand retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series rose slightly from t-2w to t-0w while remaining far below baseline
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain flat or fall for four weeks while RETAIL_REC does not weaken relative to the last 28 days, the commuting-channel hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility captures more time spent at home and less discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC will stay lower over the next two weeks rather than rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed elevated at 17.4 to 20.0 above baseline across the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean within two weeks, the home-stay suppression mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below its current near-minus-60 level will be a threshold signal of tighter movement restrictions, and RETAIL_REC will fall within one week as nonessential trips are curtailed.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -59.1 at t-0w and had recently been as low as -64.3
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -65 week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week, the restriction-threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL move together, weekend time shifts toward local outdoor activity and away from shopping streets; that substitution reduces RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both remained well below and above baseline, respectively, through the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS stays depressed and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated yet RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior 28-day average over the next month, the substitution hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM typically precedes broader errand resumption; if it continues rising from the latest week, RETAIL_REC will improve over the next two weeks as shopping trips spill over into retail visits.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -39.4 at t-2w to -31.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 28 days within two weeks, the errand-spillover hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES recovery stalls while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, household substitution into staying home dominates and retail demand weakens over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES fails to rise above -50 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +15
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was still around -53 and RESIDENTIAL around +17 to +20 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below -50 and RESIDENTIAL above +15 but RETAIL_REC increases over the next month, the home-versus-work substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stop deteriorating and begin recovering together, the metro is moving into a looser mobility regime that should lift RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week after being below -55
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved modestly from t-2w to t-0w but stayed deeply negative
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve from sub-55 lows yet RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week, the loosening-regime signal fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remain deeply negative while GROCERY_PHARM trends upward, households are replacing discretionary outings with essential trips only, which keeps RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed near -59 to -64 while GROCERY_PHARM improved to -31.4 by t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stay depressed and GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean within two weeks, the essential-trip substitution hypothesis fails.
